claims.claim: GDPx v1.0 has 206 tasks across 11 domains built with 14 partners; Claude Opus 5.5 leads at 12.0, Gemini 4 Carbon 10.9, GPT-6 Astra 9.6.
GDPx task counts per domain: RSI 10, chip design 34, cyber 18, bio 13, finance 24, legal 20, quant 10, hardware 21, materials 23, alignment 18, SWE 15.
GDPx weights all domains equally and partners equally within a domain; the headline is pass@1 across three attempts with an 8-hour default limit.
Opus 5.5 averaged $51.41 per task and 548K output tokens on GDPx; Gemini 4 Carbon $16.29; GPT-6 Astra $53.99.
Excluding cyber, bio and alignment, GPT-6 Astra scores 11.8 and Opus 5.5 11.7, and Gemini 4 Carbon slips from second to fifth.
Claude Opus 5.5 is priced at $4 per million input and $20 per million output tokens, with cache reads at $0.20.
Anthropic states that Opus 5.5 cyber tasks flagged by classifiers fall back to Opus 4.8 and that this likely reduces its benchmark scores.
GPT-6.1 Sol scored 8.4 at $9.80 per task; DeepSeek 4.1 Flash 5.4 at $0.94; GPT-6 Luna 5.1 at $0.92; Fable 5.1 8.5 at $67.16; Sonnet 5.5 8.2 at $45.27; Grok 4.7 3.9 at $16.34.
Gemini 4 Carbon was announced 2026-10-28 with first access limited to cyber defenders in the Fairwind Program and is not generally available.
Gemini 4 Argon is $2/$10 per million input/output tokens through 2026-11-30 and $4/$20 from 2026-12-01; Carbon is not on Google's pricing page.
GPT-6 Astra is $10/$50, GPT-6.1 Sol $2/$10 and GPT-6 Luna $0.10/$0.50 per million input/output tokens, with higher rates above 272K input tokens.
GDPval has 1,320 tasks across 44 occupations in 9 sectors, a 220-task gold subset, and human inter-rater agreement of about 71%.
Clustered standard errors on popular evals can be over three times naive standard errors, and frontier models' question scores correlate 0.3 to 0.7.
Switching scaffold alone moves SWE-bench Verified scores by up to 11 points for GPT-5 and 15 for Kimi K2 Thinking.
In Fleet's cyber alignment tasks 196 of 200 runs broke at least one behavior rule and 173 broke a rule rated severely misaligned.
SemiAnalysis says Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra have sandbagged overall scores due to safety classifiers, and that Muse Wonder Full is the best available cyber model.
Sundar Pichai posted that GDPx is a high-quality benchmark with headroom and pointed to the cost line for Carbon.
Partner sections of the GDPx post were largely written by the partners, and SemiAnalysis says it wanted chip design slightly overrepresented.
Finance and legal tasks score essentially 0 for every model under binary grading, so GDPx reports average partial scores for them.
SemiAnalysis's QA process flags nearly 50% of Terminal Bench 4.0 tasks as broken.
Epoch reports RL-environment task prices mostly of $200 to $2,000 and benchmarking demand far below RL-training demand.
Implied Opus 5.5 average across cyber, bio and alignment is about 12.8 points.
assumptions: Alternate ranking uses equal weights over the remaining 8 domains
